absent: Real behavior of PCI, platform and reserved memory helpers when device-tree support is enabled, including locking and error paths.
Numeric values, lookup helpers and string forms for the OID enumeration.
Implementation and locking of the once start and finish helpers referenced by the once macros.
Runtime packing and unpacking function signatures, buffer ownership and concurrency rules.
Device-tree node, device and resource structure layouts and lifetime rules beyond the field names used here.

findings.text: In the configuration covered here the PCI device-tree helpers are inert with fixed outcomes. Child lookup reports absence, devfn query reports EINVAL, IRQ mapping reports zero, while probe-only handling and wake GPIO setup and teardown have no observable effect.

In the configuration shown the platform device-tree helpers are inert. Node to device translation and device creation report absence, destruction and both population forms plus the device-managed population form report ENODEV, and both depopulation forms have no effect.
Auxiliary matching data holds compatible and phys_addr and name and platform_data. The first and third are strings, the second is a resource sized address and the last is an opaque pointer.
A table initializer builds one auxiliary entry from compatibility, address, name and platform data values supplied in caller order, suitable for static lookup tables.

A reserved region descriptor carries name and ops and base and size and priv. The name is a string, ops points to a callback table, base and size use physical address units, and priv is an opaque pointer for the owning implementation.

The callback table defines node_validate and node_fixup and node_init and device_init and device_release. Validation can propose alignment, fixup receives chosen base and size, init receives a tree offset with a descriptor, and the device hooks receive a descriptor with a device.

Region drivers register through a declaration parameterized by symbolic name, compatibility string and operations pointer. Two spellings exist for enabled versus disabled configurations, one emitting a real table entry and one emitting a placeholder.

When support is unavailable the reserved memory helpers have fixed outcomes. Indexed and named device init report ENOSYS, device-managed init reports EOPNOTSUPP, lookup reports absence, region to resource conversions report ENOSYS, region counting reports zero, and release has no effect.
The generic device init is defined as indexed init on the own tree node at index zero, so its contract matches that specialization.

A single enumeration assigns small integer handles to well known object identifiers spanning public key algorithms, hashes including SHA-2 and SHA-3 families, certificate attributes and extensions, authentication mechanisms, code signing, GOST, SM series, TPM key types and ML-DSA. A final member OID__NR marks the table size.

The once helper runs a caller supplied routine at most once per expansion site and reports whether this call performed the run. State is a per-site persistent flag kept in a dedicated data section plus a per-site static key enabling a fast path after completion, with interrupt-safe start and finish coordination and module ownership tracking.

A sleepable variant provides the same at-most-once per-site guarantee with sleepable start and finish coordination. Convenience wrappers apply both forms to one-time random filling of a caller buffer.

A lightweight family provides conditional one-time execution per expansion site. One form always attempts the call, one form gates on a caller condition, and the shared predicate tracks a per-site persistent flag in a dedicated section and reports whether this call is the first passing one.
The lightweight predicate performs a plain check and set of its flag with no exclusion shown, so concurrent first arrivals in multiple contexts may both observe first-run status.

A generator defines a descriptor type for one integer width holding startbit and endbit and offset and size. An entry initializer derives offset and size from a structure and member pair together with caller supplied bit bounds.

Compile time checks constrain each descriptor and table. Start is ordered above end, storage size is one of one two four or eight, bit span fits within storage, ordering across consecutive entries is strictly monotonic in the direction set by the first two entries, neighbors do not overlap, buffer length is a compile time constant, and first and last entries lie inside the buffer.

Packing behavior selects three independent quirk bits occupying the lowest three bit positions for most-significant-bit placement, little endian handling and 32-bit word order, plus a two-valued operation selector with members PACK and UNPACK.

Numbered check wrappers cumulatively validate table prefixes by invoking the previous prefix check and then the single entry check for the next index, supporting tables from one through fifty entries, with a generic selector dispatching on table length.

Fallback shims return generic absence or unsupported outcomes that are indistinguishable from runtime lookup failures, so callers cannot tell disabled build configuration from missing hardware from return values alone.
Each public header is protected by a conventional include guard macro that prevents multiple inclusion within one translation unit.
